title: Runtime compatibility contract: deprecation signaling, negotiation headers, and canary upgrade tooling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Define a machine-readable runtime compatibility contract and associated operational conventions for signaling deprecations, negotiating feature compatibility, and driving automated canary upgrades. This ticket establishes the spec for a runtime-compat manifest, HTTP negotiation headers, deprecation TTL policy, and the minimum product and tooling changes required to safely ship breaking and non-breaking changes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Why: Upgrades are a frequent source of customer incidents. We currently lack a single source-of-truth for what runtime features/behaviors are guaranteed across versions and no standardized signal for clients to gracefully degrade when a feature is removed. A compact, machine-readable contract plus upgrade preflight tooling will reduce outages during rollouts and enable safer automation (canaries, auto-rollbacks, staged migrations).

Scope:
- Define "runtime-compat" manifest format (version, capability flags, deprecated_features list, removal_dates). Manifest must be retrievable from the control plane and optionally served by on-prem runtimes at /.well-known/runtime-compat.
- Define HTTP negotiation headers: X-Redwood-Runtime-Version, X-Redwood-Compat-Mode, and X-Redwood-Deprecation-Warning (server-sent).
- Deprecation policy: features marked deprecated in a MINOR release remain supported for at least two MINOR cycles or 180 days (whichever is longer) before removal; exceptional removals require explicit customer opt-in and an extended deprecation window.
- Define compatibility modes: strict (error on incompatible calls), tolerant (warnings via headers/logs), and shim (server applies compatibility fallback).
- Implement an "rwd-upgrade-check" CI/CLI tool that validates a client or operator's integration against a target runtime-compat manifest via handshake tests and schema linting.
- Console integration: surface manifest differences in rollouts UI and gate canary promotion on compatibility metrics (errors, latency, regression to golden prompts).
- Provide SDK guidance: default to tolerant mode and surface deprecation warnings to application logs; provide opt-in strict enforcement for infra teams.
acceptance_criteria:
1) runtime-compat manifest v1 spec doc merged in confluence and approved by Release Eng and API Product.
2) Control plane exposes manifests for hosted runtimes and instructions for customers to host /.well-known/runtime-compat for private deployments.
3) HTTP negotiation headers implemented in runtime and SDKs; deprecation warnings emitted for two staged deprecations in runtime-2.0 branch.
4) rwd-upgrade-check CLI exists with tests that can detect a breaking change in a mock consumer and returns non-zero exit code on incompatibility.
4b) CI job template provided for repos to run upgrade-check against designated runtime images.
5) Console rollout UI shows 'compat delta' and blocks canary promotion if error budget burn or compatibility test failures exceed thresholds.
6) Documentation + SDK examples updated (JS/Python) demonstrating compatibility mode usage and how to consume deprecation headers.
tasks: Draft runtime-compat manifest schema and examples
Add runtime header emission and deprecation warning logic
Implement /.well-known runtime-compat serving for Private control plane
Build rwd-upgrade-check CLI and CI template
Console: show manifest delta and add gate hook
SDK: surface deprecation headers and add compatibility mode flag
Write Confluence runbook for handling accelerated removals and emergency opt-in
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: Strict default would force safer clients but raise upgrade friction for internal rapid experiments; chosen default is 'tolerant' for developer ergonomics with an opt-in strict mode for infra tenants.
- We avoid binary-embedding of manifest into released images to permit runtime feature toggles without rebuilds; manifests are canonical control-plane artifacts.
- Two-cycle deprecation window balances customer stability vs. ability to iterate; legal/enterprise customers can request extended timelines via support SLA.
- For on-prem/private, we provide a manual import script and recommend a weekly manifest sync schedule to handle air-gapped environments.
- Edge case: KV cache format changes may require a migration utility; migration strategy will be a follow-up ticket (ENG-50901).
